topics.name: US-China Trade War and Market Turmoil
topics.summary: Global markets fell sharply amid renewed US-China trade tensions; S&P 500 and Dow down over 10% YTD, NASDAQ down 3.5% on the day. Nvidia warned billions lost from export restrictions. The 'sell America' trade resumed with gold hitting records and bonds selling off.

topics.name: Federal Reserve Independence Threat
topics.summary: Reports that Trump threatened to fire Fed Chair Jerome Powell spooked markets; discussed the Fed's limited control over the long end of the yield curve and the 10-year Treasury as the key economic signal that has moved opposite to administration goals.

topics.name: Bitcoin Decoupling from Risk Assets
topics.summary: Tyler Winklevoss posted that Bitcoin was not falling in lockstep with equities, suggesting maturation as a store of value; Bitcoin down 7% YTD but up ~2% on the day despite heavy NASDAQ selling. Hosts plan a dedicated crypto day.

topics.name: Pope Francis Death and Legacy
topics.summary: Pope Francis died Easter Monday at 88; the WSJ obituary praised his concern for the poor but criticized his radical environmentalism, anti-Americanism, and the Vatican deal giving the CCP influence over bishop selection, calling him a pope from progressivism's weakest markets.

topics.name: Political Polarization Economics
topics.summary: Roland Fryer's WSJ op-ed research showed people interpret ambiguous signals as confirming prior beliefs, causing polarization to compound even with neutral information exposure. Over half of 600 test subjects emerged with more extreme views; the finding partly exonerates Facebook's filter bubble.

topics.name: Automation of Shoe Manufacturing
topics.summary: Nike, Under Armour, and Adidas all attempted and failed to automate footwear production at scale due to soft materials, temperature variance, and SKU diversity; leaves all three exposed to tariffs on Vietnam, China, and Indonesia with no near-term automation solution.

topics.name: China Humanoid Robot Half Marathon
topics.summary: 21 humanoid robot models raced in Beijing; TianKong Ultra finished in 2:40:42 vs. human winner's 1:02:36, requiring three battery swaps and human joystick operators. China is targeting world robotics leadership by 2027 with heavy government subsidies.

topics.name: Re-industrialization and US Manufacturing Viability
topics.summary: Tariffs are stress-testing manufacturing revival; consensus is that robotics automation isn't ready to replace Asian labor at the speed tariff timelines demand. Companies like Machina Labs are early movers but factory build-outs take years, not quarters.

topics.name: Supplement and Gummy Startup Boom
topics.summary: Gruns raising at $500M valuation; Create Wellness at ~$25M ARR pace with creatine gummies; Ozempic users emerging as new TAM for micronutrient gummies. The American consumer continues to be 'undefeated' in supplement spending.

topics.name: Early-Stage Venture Market
topics.summary: Box Group's David Tisch argues seed-stage investing is largely decoupled from macro via the accordion effect; AI now dominates 90-170% of pitches vs. 30-40% two years ago; M&A remains the missing liquidity mechanism; LP patience strained by 12-15 year real fund timelines.

topics.name: AI Investing Thesis and Enterprise Adoption
topics.summary: Mike Vernal argues best AI companies build down from deep customer understanding; large tech is too risk-averse to ship great AI products, opening startup opportunities; M&A should accelerate as big-tech valuations enable meeting founder price expectations.

topics.name: RL Scaling as the Key 2025 AI Vector
topics.summary: William Brown argues reinforcement learning—not more pre-training data—is the dominant 2025 scaling approach; DeepSeek proved this early; OpenAI is betting on agentic RL; diminishing economic returns on raw compute for pure transformer pre-training.

topics.name: OpenAI Acquiring Windsurf
topics.summary: Reports that OpenAI is looking to buy Windsurf for ~$3B; seen as signal of friction with Microsoft's Copilot and desire for a dedicated enterprise coding product; raises debate about whether an M&A era for AI application-layer companies is beginning.

topics.name: AI Email and Horizontal AI Products Opportunity
topics.summary: Mike Vernal argues no great AI email client exists despite 21 years of Gmail data being available; large tech companies are too conservative; startups can win horizontal AI assistant experiences that foundation model providers won't prioritize.

topics.name: Cluely Launch and AI-Assisted Cognition
topics.summary: Roy launched Cluely, an AI that sees your screen and feeds real-time answers, on Easter Sunday; raised $5M; 4.3M launch video views; framed as the 'calculator moment' for AI-assisted cognition with a 'cheat on everything' manifesto.

topics.name: Machina Labs and Advanced Defense Manufacturing
topics.summary: Machina Labs is using robotic dieless sheet forming and AI to create a 'robotic craftsman'; working with missile manufacturers on hypersonics-relevant materials like titanium; Golden Dome program may represent ~7% of DOD budget and is a major opportunity.

topics.name: DeepSeek Engineering Efficiency Lessons
topics.summary: DeepSeek's advantage was not any single innovation but ~10-15 stacked optimizations that compounded; their free chat serving all of China on 2,000 GPUs is embarrassing Western AI providers on inference efficiency and has prompted OpenAI to recruit HFT engineers.

topics.name: M&A Drought in Tech and Path to Revival
topics.summary: David Tisch and Mike Vernal agreed that government regulatory overreach (e.g., blocking Plaid acquisition) and valuation mismatches killed a decade of tech M&A; both are cautiously optimistic that high big-tech valuations and AI urgency could unlock a new M&A cycle.
